```markdown
# Breaking-change flag in release notes

Source: `specs/deferred_items.md`, item 7.

## Goal

Mark breaking changes in the output of `release-notes`. Readers must see them at a glance. `announce` must list them first in its post.

## Format

`release-notes` writes one bullet for each merged pull request. A bullet for a breaking pull request starts with the tag `[breaking]` and one space, after the list marker. The rest of the bullet does not change.

A pull request is breaking when it has the `breaking` label. No other source sets the tag.

Bullets without the tag keep the current format. Release notes that were written before this change stay valid.

## Components

1. `skills/release-notes/SKILL.md`: add the rule that writes `[breaking] ` at the start of a bullet when the pull request has the `breaking` label.
2. `skills/changelog-check/parse.py`: before the split on " — ", remove a leading `[breaking] ` from the bullet text. Set `breaking=True` on that entry. Set `breaking=False` on all other entries. The rule that rejects a bullet with more than two parts does not change, and it applies to the text after the tag is removed.
3. `skills/announce/SKILL.md`: list breaking entries first. Keep the original order inside the breaking group and inside the other group.

## Tag matching

The match is exact and case-sensitive: `[breaking]` followed by one space, at the start of the bullet text. Other text, for example `[Breaking]` or a `[breaking]` in the middle of the bullet, is not a tag. `parse.py` leaves that text in the bullet unchanged.

## Testing

Add a test in `skills/changelog-check/`:

- A tagged bullet parses to an entry with `breaking=True`. The tag is not in the parsed fields.
- An untagged bullet parses to the same fields as before, with `breaking=False`.

## Out of scope

- Other flags or tags.
- Detection of breaking changes from code or commit messages.
```

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The tag goes in front of the bullet, so `parse.py` can remove it before the split on " — ". The rule that rejects more than two parts then stays unchanged. That is why older notes stay valid.
- An exact, case-sensitive match keeps the parser strict. A tag such as `[Breaking]` stays in the bullet text, so a person can see the error in the output.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

- `announce` keeps the original order inside each group.
